sources.entry: claude-code-docs by Constantin Shafranski - A mirror of the Anthropic&copy; PBC documentation site for Claude/Code, but with bonus features like full-text search and query-time updates - up-to-the-minute, fully-indexed information so that Claude Code can read about itself.

summary.one_liner: A metadata-only index and bash client that lets Claude Code fetch live Anthropic Claude and Claude Code documentation pages on demand, with full-text search, interactive HTML courses, and changelog reports.
summary.what_it_does: The repository commits only a page manifest and a prose-free search index (about 3 MB), not the documentation text itself. A bash, curl, and jq client searches that index and downloads the matching .md pages directly from Anthropic's servers into a local cache. A SessionStart hook syncs metadata and re-fetches changed pages each session. The /docs skill supports direct lookups, natural-language queries, and auto-discovery, where Claude reads relevant docs before answering. The skill can also generate a self-contained animated HTML course on a topic and produce an HTML changelog report of added, changed, and removed doc pages over a chosen time window. The README says it covers platform.claude.com and code.claude.com, with CI regenerating the index every 3 hours.
use_cases: Grounding Claude Code answers in current official docs
Looking up Claude API, Agent SDK, or hooks documentation from the terminal
Generating an interactive HTML course on a Claude topic
Tracking what changed in Anthropic's docs over the last day, week, or month
Sharing a consistent docs setup with a team via project settings
notable: Commits zero documentation prose; fetches each page from Anthropic on demand instead of mirroring
Requires only bash, curl, and jq with no MCP server or API keys
Auto-discovery reads relevant docs without a command prefix
Generates self-contained interactive HTML courses saved locally
Fail-closed CI safeguards and domain-allowlisted, HTTPS-only fetching
caveats: Requires jq, which is not preinstalled everywhere (brew or apt install)
Script install path is a legacy option; the README recommends the plugin instead
Documentation content belongs to Anthropic; only the tool code is open source under MIT
